$comment: Branching stories (kind 'story'). Each node: text, speaker, mood, choices [{text, next, points, feedback}]. A node with no choices ends the story. Score = points earned / maxPoints.

a.speaker: Max
a.text: Hi! My bike is broken and I need to get to soccer. Can I borrow yours today? I'll bring it back by dinner.

choices.text: Sure! Please bring it back by dinner.
choices.feedback: Lending to a friend with a clear plan is kind and fair.

choices.text: Only if you pay me $50 for the afternoon.
choices.feedback: That's way too much for one afternoon! Fair deals matter.

b.speaker: Narwhal
b.text: Max brought your bike back right on time, clean and safe! Next week Max asks to borrow it again.

choices.text: Yes! Max kept the promise last time.
choices.feedback: Exactly! When people pay back on time, we trust them more. Banks work the same way with credit.

choices.text: No, I don’t want to lend it ever again.
choices.feedback: That's okay, but Max proved they're trustworthy. Trust grows when promises are kept.

b2.speaker: Max
b2.text: Fifty dollars?! That's more than a new tire costs. I'll ask someone else…

choices.text: Okay, okay, you can borrow it for free if you bring it back by dinner.
choices.feedback: Being fair helps everyone.

c.speaker: Narwhal
c.text: Here's the big idea: when grown-ups borrow from a bank and pay back ON TIME, the bank trusts them more and lends at a lower cost. That trust is called CREDIT. Which friend would a bank trust more?

choices.text: A friend who always pays back on time
choices.feedback: Yes! Paying back on time builds good credit.

choices.text: A friend who forgets to pay back
choices.feedback: Forgetting to pay back hurts trust (and credit). On-time is the key!

end.speaker: Narwhal
end.text: Great thinking! Borrowing is a promise. Keep your promises and people (and banks) will trust you.

a.speaker: Narwhal
a.text: You made $30 at your lemonade stand! What do you do first?

choices.text: Put some in my Save jar
choices.feedback: Paying yourself first is a great habit!

choices.text: Spend it all on candy
choices.feedback: Candy is fun, but then nothing is left for later.

b.speaker: Narwhal
b.text: Your lemons cost $10. How much profit did you really make?

choices.feedback: Right! $30 − $10 = $20 profit.
Remember to subtract what you spent on lemons: $30 − $10 = $20.

c.speaker: Narwhal
c.text: A friend says: give me your $20 and I'll give you $100 next week! What do you do?

choices.text: No thanks, that’s too good to be true
choices.feedback: Smart! Promises of huge, fast money are usually tricks.

choices.text: Yes! Here’s my $20, I can’t wait for $100!
choices.feedback: Careful! If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is.

end.speaker: Narwhal
end.text: Save some, know your profit, and watch out for tricks. You're a smart business owner!

a.speaker: Narwhal
a.text: You got your first paycheck from the bakery: $80! Your favorite shoes are $75. What's your plan?

choices.text: Save some, buy the shoes in a few weeks
choices.feedback: Planning big wants is smart.

choices.text: Buy the shoes right now and spend the rest too
choices.feedback: Okay, but now there's only $5 left for anything else.

b.speaker: Narwhal
b.text: Your little brother's birthday is next week. You'd like to get him a gift.

choices.text: Plan $10 for a gift from my paycheck
choices.feedback: Sharing is part of a good budget!

choices.text: Borrow money for a gift
choices.feedback: Borrowing for gifts can get tricky. Planning ahead works better.

c.speaker: Narwhal
c.text: Your boss offers more hours next month. That means less free time but more money. What do you think?

choices.text: Take a few extra hours and save for my goal
choices.feedback: Balancing time and money is a real trade-off. Nice!

choices.text: Work every free minute, even on school nights
choices.feedback: Money matters, but so do rest and friends. Balance is key!

end.speaker: Narwhal
end.text: You planned for wants, shared with family, and thought about time vs. money. That's real money wisdom!

a.speaker: Mayor Penny
a.text: The town wants a new playground. Where should the money come from?

choices.text: Everyone chips in a little through taxes
choices.feedback: Yes! Taxes let a whole town build things together.

choices.text: One kid pays for all of it
choices.feedback: That would be unfair and way too expensive for one person.

b.speaker: Mayor Penny
b.text: Which of these is paid for with taxes?

choices.text: Firefighters
choices.feedback: Right! Firefighters keep everyone safe.

choices.text: My new video game
choices.feedback: Families buy their own games. Taxes pay for things everyone shares.

c.speaker: Mayor Penny
c.text: Your paycheck says 'Earned $100, Take home $90.' Where did $10 go?

choices.text: Taxes for roads, schools and parks
choices.feedback: Exactly! That's why take-home pay is smaller.

choices.text: It disappeared because of a bank mistake
choices.feedback: It went to taxes, which pay for things we all use.

end.speaker: Narwhal
end.text: Taxes are how a community buys things together. Now you know where the money goes!
